business_problem: Trend Micro needed a way to deploy its proprietary cybersecurity LLMs securely and quickly across cloud, hybrid, and on-premises environments while preserving data sovereignty, zero-trust controls, observability, and control over sensitive telemetry and intellectual property.
solution_summary: Trend Micro uses its proprietary Trend Cybertron cybersecurity LLM together with the NVIDIA universal LLM NIM microservice to operationalize secure AI inference on NVIDIA Enterprise AI factories. The implementation is built around security-specific inputs including risk intelligence, customer telemetry, adversarial tactics, MITRE ATT&CK techniques, SIEM logs, natural-language risk reports, red-team narratives, security knowledge bases, and threat intelligence. The universal LLM NIM microservice serves Cybertron in cloud, hybrid, and on-premises deployments and abstracts inference backends so Trend can run NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM for high-performance inference or vLLM for throughput and batching. Trend pairs this serving layer with the AI-Q Blueprint to build RAG-style security agents that reason over knowledge bases and telemetry in real time, while NVIDIA NeMo Data Flywheel is used to monitor inference behavior and retrain models to manage drift and sustain accuracy.

solution_components.name: Trend Cybertron
solution_components.role: Trend Micro's domain-specific cybersecurity LLM analyzes security language, logs, risk reports, and adversarial tactics for proactive cyber defense.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA universal LLM NIM microservice
solution_components.role: It packages and deploys Cybertron for rapid, backend-agnostic, secure inference across cloud, hybrid, and on-premises environments.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA Enterprise AI factories
solution_components.role: They provide the infrastructure environments where Trend runs its custom Cybertron models.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM
solution_components.role: It is one of the inference backends Trend can choose for high-performance Cybertron inference.

solution_components.name: vLLM
solution_components.role: It is an alternative inference backend used for throughput and batching behind the NIM deployment model.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA NeMo Data Flywheel
solution_components.role: It supports production inference monitoring and retraining workflows to reduce model drift over time.

solution_components.name: AI-Q Blueprint
solution_components.role: It is integrated with NIM to build security AI agents that reason over knowledge bases, telemetry logs, and threat intelligence in real time.

data_flow: Trend feeds Trend Cybertron with security data such as risk intelligence, telemetry, MITRE ATT&CK techniques, SIEM logs, risk reports, red-team narratives, knowledge bases, and threat intelligence. Cybertron is served through the NVIDIA universal LLM NIM microservice on NVIDIA Enterprise AI factories, using TensorRT-LLM or vLLM as the inference backend. AI-Q Blueprint then enables agents to reason over those live security sources, while NVIDIA NeMo Data Flywheel monitors production behavior and retrains models as needed.
business_outcome: Trend Micro reports faster and more flexible deployment of private cybersecurity LLMs, support for sovereign and zero-trust inference, real-time security reasoning over enterprise knowledge and telemetry, and improved ability to experiment and respond during live risks.
